title: Finding win-win solutions in Luisita
primary_topics: Three practical blocks preventing farmworker-beneficiaries from actually benefiting from the Luisita ruling
CJ's argument that the 10-year ban on selling parcels should start from SDP stock issuance, not from unissued CLOAs
Proposal to allow FWBs to sell parcels to reputable developers via a Supreme Court-tossed RTC venue for win-win compromise
sub_topics: Social justice as giving the means AND freedom to lift oneself out of destitution -- not just legal rights

SCTex paid P1 million/hectare (P100/sq m) -- decade later; gross disparity

stances.claim: The 10-year ban on selling FWB parcels should be counted from the issuance of SDP shares — which happened more than 10 years ago — not from the issuance of CLOAs/EPs which have never been issued, because the shares were the equivalent of the EP/CLOA under the peculiar SDP facts.
stances.rhetorical_move: equitable-equivalence argument: the SDP shares as the functional equivalent of CLOAs, triggering the same legal period

stances.claim: The Supreme Court should allow FWBs to sell their parcels to reputable developers — the means given them to rise from destitution — because strict enforcement of the anti-alienation rule serves no protective purpose for FWBs who are already rights-conscious and have been litigating for decades.
stances.rhetorical_move: protective-purpose-exhaustion argument: the rule's protective rationale is defeated when its beneficiaries are experienced litigants, not naive newcomers

stances.claim: The Court should toss the just compensation issue to the Regional Trial Court — per Justice Bersamin's suggestion — to give the parties the opportunity to find win-win solutions freely and voluntarily, consistent with the hacienda's proximity to the Diosdado Macapagal Airport making it a valuable multi-use development site.
stances.rhetorical_move: forum-transfer recommendation: RTC as the optimal venue for market-driven voluntary compromise over court-imposed valuation

notable_anecdotes: The SCTex price paradox: the court-fixed 1989 just compensation at P40,000/hectare (P4/sq m) while the SCTex bought 80 hectares of the same hacienda a decade later at P1 million/hectare (P100/sq m) — a 25-fold price gap within the same estate that CJ deploys as the most visceral evidence of the 1989 valuation date's injustice to both parties.

The .62 hectare per FWB calculation — on soil that is 'not uniform: some part is rocky, some clayish, some flooded, some steep and elevated' — making the abstract 'land-to-the-tillers' victory concretely insufficient for viable farming, and the practical argument for allowing resale.

The Canlubang Sugar Estate analogy: proper planning could transform Hacienda Luisita into a multi-use hub of commerce, industry, and agriculture 'similar to the Canlubang Sugar Estate in Laguna' — used as a concrete real-world model of the win-win development path CJ envisions.

one_paragraph_summary: A week after the SC's November 22, 2011 resolution unanimously ordering the parceling of Hacienda Luisita among 6,296 FWBs, Panganiban identifies three practical blocks that prevent the social justice victory from actually reaching the farmworkers. First, each FWB gets only .62 hectares (6,200 sq m) of non-uniform soil -- rocky, clayish, flooded, or steep -- too small for viable farming. Second, just compensation is fixed at the 1989 market value of P40,000/hectare (P4/sq m), despite the SCTex buying 80 hectares of the same estate a decade later at P1 million/hectare (P100/sq m), with decades of further litigation before finalization. Third, the 10-year ban on selling parcels has not yet begun because no CLOAs or EPs have been issued -- CJ argues it should instead be counted from the SDP stock issuance (more than 10 years ago), the functional equivalent of a CLOA, since the FWBs are already experienced litigants who are conscious of their rights (per Justice Sereno) and do not need the rule's protective purpose. He recommends allowing FWBs to sell their parcels to reputable developers (Ayala, Robinsons, Megaworld) after the SC follows Justice Bersamin's suggestion of tossing the just compensation issue to the RTC for voluntary win-win negotiation -- citing the Diosdado Macapagal Airport 20 minutes away and the Canlubang Sugar Estate in Laguna as a model for what the hacienda could become as a multi-use hub of commerce, industry, and agriculture.
